FANTASY CRUX LITE
LITE RULES
FANTASY CRUX LITE

The whole game in a few pages, for fast play and convention tables.

WHAT IS LITE?

Fantasy Crux is a gritty percentile game about capable adventurers. Violence is dangerous, preparation matters, and Hero Points leave room for epic reversals.

Lite is the same game with its side rules folded together. Almost everything is a skill test, and almost every special case is a reason to add Bonus or Penalty dice. An experienced Gamemaster can read it in an evening and run it from memory.

USING LITE

Lite keeps the same numbers as the full rules: characteristics, skills, weapons, armour, wounds and Shaping. Characters, creatures and adventures for Fantasy Crux 2.0 work in Lite unchanged, and so do any Talents a character has.

When Lite is silent, use the full rules at fantasycrux.org, or make a quick ruling and keep playing.

YOU NEED

Two ten-sided dice for percentile rolls, one for tens and one for units, plus a few spare ten-sided dice for Bonus and Penalty dice. A D4, D6, D8, D10 and D12 for damage. A character sheet and a pencil for each player.

CONTENTS
Play and Circumstances: tests and the dice that modify them.
Characters and Edges and Growth: build and improve a character.
Combat and More Combat: fights, wounds and healing.
Equipment and Adventuring: gear, travel and hazards.
Shaping: magic, in two pages.
Gamemaster: running tests, quick NPCs and common creatures.
FANTASY CRUX LITE · 2.0 BETA
PAGE 1

FANTASY CRUX LITE
PLAY
PLAY

Say what you try. Roll only when failure would matter.

MAKE A TEST
Say what your character wants and how they try.
The GM names the skill and any Bonus or Penalty dice. Routine and impossible tasks need no roll.
Roll D100: a tens die and a units die read 01 to 100; 00 is 100. A result at or under the skill succeeds.
Apply the result and play on. Do not repeat the test until something changes.
RESULT GRADES
Roll	Grade
01 to the skill's tens digit	Critical: success with an extra benefit.
At or under the skill	Success.
Over the skill	Failure.
99–00; only 00 at 100%	Fumble: failure with a consequence fitting the risk.

A 59% skill is Critical on 01–05; any skill above 0% is Critical on 01. A Fumble overrides success. Skills never exceed 100%.

A Critical succeeds especially quickly, thoroughly or well, and can reveal something extra. A Fumble adds a serious consequence that follows from the risk: lost time, broken gear, danger or a worse position.

BONUS AND PENALTY DICE

Each +1B adds one tens die and you keep the best result; each -1P adds one and you keep the worst. Pair every tens die with the same units die. Cancel them one for one and keep at most +3B or -3P.

Best result: the higher grade first (Critical, Success, Failure, Fumble). Among successes the higher roll is better; among failures, the lower.

Example. Skill 70%, +1B: units 5, tens 2 and 6 give 25 or 65. Both succeed, so keep 65.

OPPOSED TESTS

When someone resists, both roll. The higher grade wins. With the same grade, the higher success wins, or the lower failure. Still tied: the higher skill wins, then the defender; with no defender, nothing changes. Two successes of 42 and 31: 42 wins. Two failures of 72 and 85: 72 wins.

LET THE FICTION LEAD

Rules settle uncertain moments; they do not replace common sense. The GM can grant dice for a strong advantage, rule that size or anatomy makes an action impossible, or let an obvious approach succeed without a roll. Say so before the roll.

HELP

Helpers who know the job, with 26% or more in the skill, give +1B in total, not per helper. Exceptional teamwork can give +2B.

GROUP TESTS

If one failure sinks everyone, such as sneaking past a guard, roll once for the weakest member. If one success is enough, such as spotting an ambush, roll once for the best, with +1B for the others' help.

HERO POINTS

Each player character starts with 2; the GM awards more for heroic play. Spend 1 to:

Reroll a failed test, before its consequences. One reroll per test.
Downgrade a Major Wound: keep the HP loss, but not Wounded or Bleeding.
Avoid Death: at 0 HP, become stable and unconscious. Wake after the scene with 1 HP.
Story benefit: with GM approval, add a plausible favourable detail.
EXAMPLE OF PLAY

Corin sneaks past a sentry at night: Deception 55% against the sentry's Perception 45%. Moonlight is partial darkness, so the sentry rolls at -1P, and Corin's dark cloak gives him +1B. Corin's dice read 25 or 65; he keeps 25, a Success. The sentry's read 38 or 78; he must keep 78, a Failure. Corin slips past.

DICE AND TIME

2D6+1 means roll two six-sided dice and add 1. Round to the nearest whole number; halves round up. A round is five seconds. A scene is one continuous situation, such as a fight, a chase or a negotiation. Distances are in metres; on a grid, a square is 2 m.

FANTASY CRUX LITE · 2.0 BETA
PAGE 2

FANTASY CRUX LITE
PLAY
CIRCUMSTANCES

Most special rules are reasons to add Bonus or Penalty dice.

ADD DICE FOR WHAT MATTERS

A clear advantage is +1B, a clear problem -1P; two dice are for strong factors. Add up different causes, but use only the strongest of one kind, such as the worst cover. Then cancel and cap at +3B or -3P. Judge new cases alike.

YOUR CONDITION
You are…	Dice
Wounded, after a Major Wound	-1P on every test
Fatigued / Exhausted	-1P / -2P on every test
Held in a grapple, or holding someone	-1P on every test
Below a weapon's STR or DEX minimum	-1P with that weapon
Overloaded: over STR + SIZ in ENC	-1P on physical tests
On unstable ground	-1P
CLOSE COMBAT
Situation	Dice
Target prone, flanked or attacked from behind	+1B to attack
You have higher ground	+1B to your own rolls
You are prone	-1P to your own rolls
Fighting underwater	-2P
Rider against someone on foot	Rider +1B; foe -1P to defend
Target helpless	Automatic Critical
SKILLS AND TASKS
Situation	Dice
Good tools: climbing kit, crowbar, lock picks	+1B
A sound plan, or real leverage	+1B
A successful related Lore test just before	+1B to one test
Skilled helpers	+1B in total
Healing without a Healing Kit	-2P
Resisting poison or disease after treatment	+1B
RANGED ATTACKS
Situation	Dice
You spent a Combat Action to Aim at the target	+1B
Beyond Range, up to twice Range	-2P
Partial / substantial cover	-1P / -2P
Target moved 10 m / 30 m since your last turn	-1P / -2P
Target partly / heavily hidden by mist, smoke or foliage	-1P / -2P
Target prone	-1P
Target helpless	+2B
You are prone	-2P
An enemy is adjacent to you	-2P per enemy
High wind / fierce wind	-1P / -3P
LIGHT

Light at the target counts for seeing and attacking; light at you, for moving. Radius: candle 1 m, torch or lantern 3 m, campfire 5 m, bonfire 10 m.

Light	Effect
Daylight, or within a light's radius	None
Partial darkness: twilight, or up to 3× a radius	-1P to sight-based Perception and attacks
Darkness: starlight, or up to 5× a radius	-2P to them; half Movement
Pitch black	Sight fails; close attacks -3P; quarter Movement

Low-Light Sight counts partial darkness as light and darkness as partial darkness. Night Vision counts natural night outdoors as light.

EXAMPLE

An archer aims at a running orc behind a low wall at dusk. Aim gives +1B; the orc moved 10 m (-1P), has partial cover (-1P) and stands in partial darkness (-1P). Net: -2P. Roll three tens dice and keep the worst result.

FANTASY CRUX LITE · 2.0 BETA
PAGE 3

FANTASY CRUX LITE
CHARACTERS
CHARACTERS

Build a character in five steps, or play a ready-made one.

1. CONCEPT

Write one sentence: who they are, what they do well and what drives them.

2. ANCESTRY AND CHARACTERISTICS

Start from your ancestry's spread and add 30 points. No score above 18; INT and SIZ at least 7, the rest at least 3. Quick human: assign 16, 14, 13, 12, 11, 10 and 10.

Ancestry	STR	CON	DEX	SIZ	INT	POW	CHA
Human	8	8	8	8	8	8	8
Elf	6	8	10	6	10	8	8
Dwarf	10	12	6	4	8	8	8
Orc	10	8	8	10	6	6	8
Goblin	6	7	12	4	9	8	10
Lizardfolk	11	8	6	8	9	7	7

Human: one extra edge. Elf: Low-Light Sight; in forests, ignore one Penalty die on Natural Lore. Dwarf: Blind Sight (heat); Earth Sense, knowing your depth and whether a cave is unstable while touching stone. Orc: Adrenaline Surge: once per fight, on becoming Wounded or Fatigued, ignore both penalties until the end of your next turn. Goblin: Blind Sight (heat). Lizardfolk: scaled hide, +1 AP that stacks with armour; a tail that gives -1P to attempts to trip, throw or push you.

Blind Sight (heat) perceives warm bodies without light, but no colour, writing or fine detail; walls and insulation block it.

3. ATTRIBUTES
Attribute	Value
Hit Points (HP)	(SIZ + CON) / 2
Major Wound Level (MWL)	HP / 2
Power Points (PP)	POW
Movement	15 m a round
Combat Order	(DEX + INT) / 2, minus armour ENC
Carrying capacity	STR + SIZ, in ENC

Damage Modifier (DM), from STR + SIZ: 1–10 -1D6; 11–15 -1D4; 16–25 +0; 26–30 +1D4; 31–45 +1D6; 46–60 +2D6; 61–75 +3D6; each 15 more, another +1D6.

4. SKILLS

Every character has every skill at its base. Add 50 points to Resistances, 50 to Combat, 50 to Knowledge and 75 to Practical skills, at most 30 to any one skill. Each Craft, Culture, Language and Lore subject is a separate skill.

Resistances	Base	Use
Dodge	DEX + 10	Avoid harm
Persistence	POW + 10	Resist fear
Resilience	CON + POW	Endure harm
Combat	Base	Use
Close Combat	DEX + STR	Weapons, shields
Ranged Combat	DEX + INT	Shoot, throw
Unarmed Combat	DEX + STR	Punch, grapple
Knowledge	Base	Use
Culture (own)	INT + 10	Customs
Culture (other)	INT	Customs
Language (own)	INT + 50	Speak
Language (other)	INT	50% is fluent
Lore (own field)	INT + 10	Study
Lore (other)	INT	Study
Natural Lore	INT + 10	Track, forage
Shaping	INT + POW	Shapers only
Practical	Base	Use
Athletics	DEX + STR	Climb, swim
Craft (trade)	INT + 10	Make, repair
Deception	DEX + INT	Sneak, hide
Driving	DEX + INT	Carts, wagons
Healing	INT + 10	Treat wounds
Influence	CHA + 10	Persuade
Mechanisms	DEX + INT	Locks, traps
Perception	INT + POW	Notice
Performance	CHA + 10	Entertain
Riding	DEX + POW	Mounts
Sailing	DEX + INT	Boats, ships
Streetwise	CHA + POW	Rumours
Trade	INT + 10	Haggle, value
5. EDGES, GEAR AND FINISH

Choose two edges, three for a human, and a starting gear package: see Edges and Growth. Name your character, then record HP, MWL, PP, DM, Combat Order, armour, weapons and 2 Hero Points.

FANTASY CRUX LITE · 2.0 BETA
PAGE 4

FANTASY CRUX LITE
CHARACTERS
EDGES AND GROWTH

Two edges make a character distinct. Adventures make them better.

EDGES

Choose two edges, or three for a human. An edge is a trained knack: most give a die or an exception in a narrow situation. An edge marked † replaces a hit's damage, and only if no Dodge or full Parry stops the hit; use one † edge per attack. Full-rules Talents also work in Lite, at their listed IP cost.

Ambusher: your first attack in a scene, from hiding against an unaware target, turns an ordinary hit into a Critical.
Battle Awareness: while you are aware of an enemy, attacks on you from the flank or behind gain no +1B.
Disarm †: knock one held item 1D6 m away.
Expertise: in one narrow use of a skill, such as climbing, sneaking, persuading, commanding, tracking, or Natural Lore in one terrain, ignore one Penalty die. It never adds a Bonus die. Take it again for another use.
Favoured Weapon: +1 damage with one type of weapon.
Field Surgeon: perform Surgery anywhere outside combat; your success ends Wounded at once.
Iron Fist: your unarmed blows deal 1D4 and count as Medium.
Killing Angle: once per round, +1D4 damage to a close or unarmed attack against a flanked, rear or unaware target; not on a Critical.
Missile Guard: no -1P when you Active Guard with a shield.
Off-Hand Mastery: no -1P on off-hand attacks and Parries.
Practised Hands: your first aid restores 1D4 + 2 HP, and you can retry a failed attempt once.
Protector: with a ready shield, spend your Reaction to Parry a hit on an adjacent ally.
Quick Reflexes: +2 Combat Order.
Rally: Combat Action: two allies who hear you gain +1B on their next test.
Rapid Shot: Combat Action and all Reactions: shoot a bow or sling twice, each at -1P.
Shaper: cast magic; see Shaping. A human can start with it.
Shield Cover: with a ready medium or large shield, ranged attacks and Shaping bolts aimed at you take -1P.
Shield Rush †: with a shield, push the target 2 m; it tests Athletics at -1P or falls prone.
Silent Step: while you move at half speed or less, anyone trying to notice you takes -1P.
Steady Casting: ignore one Penalty die from Wounded or a grapple on Shaping tests.
Trip †: knock the target prone.
STARTING GEAR

Choose one package:

leather armour, a ranged weapon, a two-handed close weapon and a dagger; or
leather armour, a shield, a ranged weapon, a one-handed close weapon and a dagger.

Everyone also has a backpack, 10 m of rope, two weeks of provisions, flint and tinder, a waterskin, and 4D6 × 10 SP.

GROWTH

After each adventure the GM awards 3 to 5 Improvement Points (IP). Spend them between adventures; unspent IP carry over.

Improvement	Cost
One skill +5%, or +3% if it is above 50%. Each skill once between adventures; never above 100%	1 IP
A new edge	3 IP
+1 to a characteristic other than SIZ, up to your ancestry's maximum	5 IP
A new Shaping cell with your specialty	2 IP
Any other cell, after an ordeal or with a master	4 IP
Become a Shaper, after an initiation	20 IP

After a characteristic rises, recalculate HP, MWL, PP, DM and Combat Order. Skills keep their current scores.

ANCESTRY MAXIMA
Ancestry	STR	CON	DEX	SIZ	INT	POW	CHA
Human	21	21	21	21	21	21	21
Elf	18	21	24	18	24	21	21
Dwarf	24	24	18	18	21	21	21
Orc	24	24	21	24	18	18	18
Goblin	18	21	24	15	24	21	21
Lizardfolk	24	24	18	21	21	21	18
BETWEEN ADVENTURES

Three months of suitable practice or study earns 1 IP, with the GM's approval.

PAGE 5

FANTASY CRUX LITE
COMBAT
COMBAT

Attack first. If it hits, an aware defender can react.

THE ROUND

A round is five seconds. When a fight starts, everyone rolls 1D10 + Combat Order once and acts from highest to lowest; ties go to the higher DEX. Each round you have:

one Combat Action: attack, Aim, grapple, cast, Intimidate, or use a skill or item;
one Movement Action: move up to your Movement, stand up, drop prone, or ready an item while moving half as far;
one Reaction: Dodge, Parry or an Opportunity Attack, when something triggers it, even on another's turn.

Unused actions are lost. Delay: act later in the round, after someone you choose.

MOVING IN A FIGHT
Option	Cost and effect
Disengage	Movement Action: move away; adjacent enemies can make an Opportunity Attack.
Withdraw	Both actions: move away without Opportunity Attacks. Keep your Reactions.
Sprint	Both actions: move twice your Movement. Your only Reaction is a Dodge.
Charge	Both actions and all Reactions: run straight at least 5 m, up to twice your Movement, and attack. +1D6 damage on a hit.
Set Weapon	Combat Action: brace a Set weapon. The first foe to Charge you before your next turn takes your attack first, at +1B.
ATTACK

Roll Close Combat for held weapons and shields, Unarmed Combat for fists, kicks and natural weapons, or Ranged Combat. Unarmed blows deal 1D3. A result at or under your skill hits, unless the defender stops it.

TWO WEAPONS

With two ready one-handed items (an empty hand counts as a fist), once per round choose one:

right after a normal close or unarmed attack, attack with the other at -1P, at no cost; or
keep the other for one extra Parry or Opportunity Attack at -1P. It cannot Dodge.
DEFEND

When an attack hits you and you are aware of it, you can spend one Reaction. One Reaction answers one attack. Your roll opposes the attack roll; the attacker does not roll again.

Dodge: if you win, the attack misses. -1P against ranged attacks. Once per round.
Parry: Close Combat with a ready weapon or shield, or Unarmed Combat against an unarmed attack. If you win, block damage by Size.
Active Guard: Parry a ranged attack. Against a thrown weapon, use a ready weapon at -1P or a shield normally; against arrows, bolts and stones, a shield only, at -1P.
PARRY SIZE

Weapons and shields are Light, Medium, Heavy or Huge. Fists, kicks, arrows, bolts and stones are Light.

Your parrying item is…	Damage blocked
The same Size or larger	All
One Size smaller	Half, rounded up
Two or more Sizes smaller	None
DAMAGE

Roll the weapon's damage. Add your Damage Modifier (DM) to close, unarmed and thrown attacks, but not to bows, crossbows or slings. Subtract a winning Parry, then the target's Armour Points (AP). The rest comes off HP. Damage and HP never go below 0.

Example. An ogre's Heavy club hits for 12. Your Medium sword Parries and blocks half: 6 remain. Leather armour (2 AP) stops 2. You lose 4 HP.

CRITICALS AND FUMBLES
A Critical hit deals maximum weapon damage plus maximum positive DM, nothing more, and ignores armour.
An ordinary successful Dodge or Parry turns a Critical hit into an ordinary one: roll damage and apply armour, but the defence blocks nothing.
A Critical defence that wins stops any hit.
A Fumble brings an immediate mishap: a dropped weapon, a fall, an opening.
FANTASY CRUX LITE · 2.0 BETA
PAGE 6

FANTASY CRUX LITE
COMBAT
MORE COMBAT

Second weapons, missiles, grapples, threats, and wounds.

OPPORTUNITY ATTACK

When an adjacent enemy moves away, or gives you a clear opening, spend your Reaction on one Close Combat attack.

SURPRISE

An unaware defender cannot React. Sneaking up is Deception against Perception. Being behind someone does not by itself make them unaware.

RANGED ATTACKS
Range: up to the weapon's Range, attack normally; up to twice its Range, at -2P; farther, you cannot hit.
Aim: Combat Action. Your next shot at that target gains +1B. You lose the Aim if you React, lose sight of the target, or do not shoot with your next Combat Action.
Reload: nock an arrow with your Movement Action, moving up to half your Movement. A light crossbow takes your Movement Action and your Reaction; a heavy crossbow takes the whole round.
Into a melee: apply cover. Only a Fumble hits someone else nearby.
At arm's length: within 2 m, a bow, crossbow, sling or javelin is a club: 1D6 + DM at -1P. Daggers, hatchets and shortspears work as close weapons.
GRAPPLE

Combat Action, with a free hand, against an adjacent target: roll Unarmed Combat. An aware target can spend its Reaction to oppose with Dodge or Parry; otherwise you only need a success. If you win, you hold the target, and while the hold lasts, both of you:

cannot take a Movement Action;
take -1P on every test; and
fight only unarmed or with a Light one-handed weapon.

Escape: Combat Action and an opposed Unarmed Combat test. The holder can let go at any time on their turn.

MOUNTED

Use the mount's Movement. Your attack skill cannot exceed your Riding. A mount untrained for battle might bolt: test Riding at the start of each round.

INTIMIDATE

Combat Action: demand surrender or retreat from one foe or a group. Oppose your Influence against the Persistence of the foe or its leader. The foe gets one modifier: at full strength +2B; outnumbering you but down 20% +1B; outnumbered and wounded -1P; lost half its HP or numbers -2P.

If you win, the GM decides how the foe gives way. The wounded might flee or surrender; healthy foes more often hesitate and lose a turn. A foe at full strength, or outnumbering you, surrenders only to a Critical against a failed roll. A fumbled Persistence breaks it at once.

MAJOR WOUNDS

One hit that deals at least your MWL after armour causes a Major Wound:

Wounded: -1P on every test.
Bleeding: lose 1 HP at the end of every round.

They do not stack, but a new Major Wound can restart Bleeding.

DYING

At 0 HP you fall unconscious and are Dying. You die at the end of the third round unless someone stabilises you.

Stabilise: an adjacent helper spends the whole round, staying put, and passes Healing; -2P without a Healing Kit. It stops Bleeding and Dying but restores no HP.

HEALING
First aid: after a fight, a patient who is not Wounded can receive one Healing attempt before their next full rest. Success restores 1D4 HP.
Surgery: a Wounded patient heals naturally only after Surgery: a Healing test in safety, outside combat. Success restores 1 HP.
Rest: with only light activity, recover CON / 4 HP a day. Wounded ends when HP rises above MWL.
Power Points: recover a quarter of your PP per two hours of rest; eight hours restores them all. At 0 PP you fall unconscious.
HERO POINTS SAVE LIVES

Spend 1 to keep a Major Wound's HP loss without Wounded or Bleeding, and 1 more at 0 HP to become stable instead of Dying. One hit can need both.

Improvised weapons deal 1 less damage. 10 arrows cost 1 SP; 10 bolts, 2 SP.

ARMOUR
Armour	AP	ENC	Cost

FANTASY CRUX LITE · 2.0 BETA
PAGE 8

FANTASY CRUX LITE
ADVENTURING
ADVENTURING

Distance, weariness, falls, fire and poison push back.

TRAVEL

A day is ten hours of travel in fair weather.

Pace	Per day	Cost
Marching	30 km	Arrive ready to fight
Hiking	50 km	A Fatigue test at day's end
Riding slowly	30 km	With pack animals or wagons
Riding	50 km	
Riding fast	90 km	Rider and mount test Fatigue at day's end

On rough ground, multiply: light brush 80%; medium brush, light woods or hills 70%; heavy woodland 50%.

Navigation: test Natural Lore once per uncertain day. A failure loses a quarter of the day's progress; a Fumble means no progress, and you are lost.

MOVING ABOUT

Climb at a quarter of your Movement where there are holds; an Athletics success doubles it. Swim at half Movement in calm water; test Athletics in currents, bad weather or under a heavy load. Jump: with a 5 m run, a success clears about twice your height across, or half your height up.

FATIGUE

After hard effort, such as a long fight, a sprint, or a hard climb or swim, the GM can call for a Fatigue test: Resilience.

State	Tests	Movement	Combat Order
Fatigued	-1P	Three-quarters	-3
Exhausted	-2P	Half	-6

Fail once to become Fatigued. More hard effort calls for another test at -1P; fail it to become Exhausted. A fumbled test knocks you out for 3D6 minutes, and you wake Fatigued. 20 - CON hours of rest, at least 1, clears either state.

LOAD

You carry up to STR + SIZ ENC freely. Above that you take -1P on physical and Fatigue tests and move at half speed. You can never carry twice that. Twenty small items in a container count as 1 ENC.

HAZARDS
Hazard	Effect
Falling	1D6 per full 3 m, ignoring armour; you land prone. If you can control the landing, an Athletics success removes 1D6, a Critical 2D6; a Fumble maximises the dice.
Fire	Each round: candle 1, torch 1D4, campfire 1D6, bonfire or burning room 2D6, lava 3D6. Metal armour does not help.
Holding breath	CON rounds; then Resilience each round at a cumulative -1P. On a failure take, each round until you reach air: water 2D6, thick smoke 1D6. Armour does not help.
Poison, disease	After the Delay, oppose your Resilience against its Potency. Lose and suffer its effect. A disease returns after each Delay until you win. Treatment first gives +1B.
Exposure, hunger, thirst	Safe for CON hours without shelter, CON days without food, CON × 2 hours without water (less in heat). After that, a daily Fatigue test at -1P and 1D6 damage for each lack.
OBJECTS

Attacks on still objects hit automatically. Subtract AP, then HP; at 0 HP the object breaks.

Object	AP	HP
Wooden chair	2	6
Wooden door	2	25
Iron door	4	75
Castle gate	4	120
USEFUL GEAR
Item	Cost
Healing Kit: five Healing attempts	25 SP
Climbing Kit: +1B to climb	25 SP
Crowbar: +1B to force	25 SP
Lock Picks: +1B to open locks	75 SP
Lantern: 3 m of light, 2 hours a flask	10 SP
Torch: 3 m of light for an hour	4 CP

Money: 10 copper pieces (CP) make 1 silver piece (SP); 10 SP make 1 gold piece (GP).

SHAPING
SHAPING

Magic is built from what you affect and what you do to it.

BECOMING A SHAPER

Shaper is a special edge. A human can start with it in place of all three edges, adding 50 fewer points to Resistance, Combat and Practical skills (at most 20 fewer from each). Others learn it in play, for 20 IP. It gives:

the Shaping skill, base INT + POW; you can add up to 30 Knowledge points;
a specialty, one Form or one Technique, and two known cells that contain it; and
Sense Magic and Dispel, which need no cell.

Your Practice is what you visibly do to cast: speech, gesture, a focus or prayer. If it is prevented, you cannot cast. Your Tell is a sign around you and your target, seen within 10 × M metres (at least 3 m). It shows magic, not its purpose.

CELLS

A cell joins a Technique (what you do) and a Form (what you affect), such as Unmake·Fire. You can cast only cells you know.

Technique	What it does
Conjure	Create things, barriers, beings
Bend	Move or control; no damage
Unmake	Damage, destroy, suppress, banish
Alter	Heal, transform, impose conditions
Ward	Protect, resist or deny
Scry	Learn, sense or speak; no change
Form	What it affects
Fire	Flame, heat and light
Water/Ice	Water, cold and ice
Air/Storm	Air, wind, sound, weather and lightning
Earth/Stone	Soil, stone and natural minerals
Flesh	Bodies, living or dead; plants
Mind	Thought, emotion, memory, senses
Force/Motion	Force, movement, weight and mass
Spirit	Souls, spirits and possession
Paths	Routes, thresholds and distance
Fate	Chance, omens and vows
RULES OF THUMB

Damage, healing and lost actions happen once; Duration never repeats them. Same-kind magic does not stack. Magic grants no extra actions or resources. Conjured things vanish when the Duration ends. Only Dispel ends active magic.

BUILD AN EFFECT

Say: using [cell], I cause [outcome] at [Range], affecting [Reach], for [Duration]. The GM confirms it before you roll.

Magnitude (M) = Intensity of each outcome + Range + Duration + Reach, +1 for Direct Harm.

Intensity (I) is an outcome's strength: see Common outcomes. Each different outcome adds its own Intensity; Range, Duration and Reach count once.

Rating	Range	Duration	Reach
0	Self, touch	Instant	One target
1	15 m	A scene, 10 min	2 targets, 3 m radius
2	50 m	To a full rest	5 targets, 10 m radius
3	Visible point	Ritual	Ritual

Instant lasts at most to the target's next turn; a full rest, at most 8 hours. Reach also limits size: 0 a person or door, 1 a wagon, 2 a room. Range 1–3 needs a clear route: seeing through a barrier is not enough. An area includes allies.

YOUR LIMITS
Shaping	Maximum I	Safe M
0–25%	1	1
26–50%	2	2
51–75%	3	3
76–99%	4	4
100%	5	5

No outcome can exceed your maximum Intensity. You can cast up to Safe M + 2, at -1P for Safe + 1 and -2P for Safe + 2. This is overreach: failing it brings Backlash. Intensity 5 or anything bigger needs a ritual (full rules).

TWO EXAMPLES

Firebolt: Unmake·Fire, 2D6 Projected Harm (I2) at 15 m (Range 1) = M3.

Stone skin for two: Ward·Earth/Stone, 4 AP against blows (I2), 15 m (Range 1), a scene (Duration 1), two allies (Reach 1) = M5.

CAST AND SUSTAIN

Pay Power Points, beat the defence, keep the magic going.

COMMON OUTCOMES

Use the lowest Intensity that covers what you want. Your cell must allow it.

Outcome	Intensity buys
Harm	I D6 damage, no DM. Choose Projected or Direct Harm.
Heal	I D4 HP; stops Bleeding and Dying. I3+ counts as Surgery. Once per subject per rest.
Protect	2 × I AP against physical or elemental harm; both: +1 I. Use it or armour, whichever is higher.
Barrier	2 × I AP and 5 × I HP; it blocks movement and attacks.
Boost, hinder	One skill: I2 +1B or -1P; I4 +2B or -2P.
Restrain	I1 prone, or half Movement for a turn; I2 hold a person or push 3 m; I3 lose a Combat Action; I4 incapacitate.
Sway a mind	I1 colour an emotion; I2 a reasonable command; I3 one against their interest; I4 full control.
Move	I2 climb, swim or walk a surface; I3 fly; I4 pass through a substance. Speed: I1 +3 m; I2 ×1.5; I3 ×2.
Senses	I1 Low-Light Sight; I2 Night Vision; I3 Blind Sight through one sense. Hide: I2 -1P to notice; I3 undetectable.
Learn	I1 a clue; I2 locate, diagnose or talk; I3 watch afar or read surface thoughts; I4 deep secrets.
Summon	A being for the Duration. I1: 3 HP, 25%, 1D3. I2: 6 HP, 1 AP, 40%, 1D6. I3: 10 HP, 2 AP, 55%, 1D8. I4: 14 HP, 3 AP, 70%, 2D6.
HARM: PROJECTED OR DIRECT

Projected Harm crosses space like an arrow: Dodge or shield Active Guard, both at -1P; cover and armour apply. Direct Harm (+1 M) arises inside chosen targets: they resist with Resilience, or Persistence for mind and soul, and a win cancels it. Only magical protection helps against it.

SENSE MAGIC AND DISPEL

Sense Magic: Combat Action and 1 PP; a Shaping test finds active magic within 15 m and its Form. Dispel: Combat Action; M is the target's M plus Range. Cast normally, then also beat a fresh Shaping roll for the original caster.

CAST

Spend your Combat Action, perform your Practice and roll Shaping. You must have PP to cover the full M. A calm, cosmetic trick (M0) is free and automatic.

Result	You pay
Critical	Half M
Success	M
Failure within Safe M	1 PP; no effect
Failure while overreaching	Half M; no effect; Backlash
Fumble	M; Backlash

Backlash (roll 1D4, or the GM chooses): 1 take M damage, ignoring armour; 2 lose M more PP; 3 a weaker version of the effect strikes you or something near; 4 become Fatigued, or one step worse.

DEFENDING AGAINST MAGIC

Each target opposes the casting roll; the Shaper must succeed and win.

Effect	Defence
A bolt at one target	Dodge -1P, or shield Active Guard -1P
An area you can avoid	Dodge -1P
A change to body or matter	Resilience; no Reaction
A change to mind or soul	Persistence; no Reaction
Willing, yourself, an object	None

A winning shield Active Guard blocks by Size. A spell's Size follows its Intensity: I1 Light, I2 Medium, I3 Heavy, I4 Huge. A Critical casting is not maximised and does not ignore armour.

KEEP IT GOING
All your ongoing effects together cannot exceed your INT in M. Dismiss one on your turn, freely.
A lasting benefit needs no action. Concentration, or directing another's body, costs your Combat Action each round; damage or distraction calls for Persistence, or it ends.
A summon follows one standing order, such as "guard me". Changing it costs your Movement Action within 15 m. Keep one fighting summon, or one controlled subject, at a time.
Held or controlled by magic? Spend a Combat Action to repeat your defence against the stored casting roll.

GAMEMASTER
GAMEMASTER

Roll when it matters, keep it moving, and let the world bite back.

WHEN TO ROLL

Roll when the outcome is uncertain and failure has a real consequence. Warn the players before a risky roll. If success would give only something minor, give it without a roll. Ask for one test for a long task, not one per step.

SETTING DIFFICULTY

There are no difficulty numbers. Most tests use the plain skill; let the situation add dice. A helpful edge is +1B, a hard task -1P, and a very hard one -2P. If it cannot fail, it succeeds; if it cannot succeed, do not roll.

MORALE

Foes want to live. When a fight turns against them, the wounded might flee or surrender, while healthy foes rarely just run. Use Intimidate when the heroes demand it.

REWARDS

Award 3 IP for modest progress, 4 for a completed adventure and 5 for a major achievement, plus a Hero Point for heroic play.

QUICK NPCS

Write a description, a level and gear: Guard 50 (Shortsword 1D6+1, Leather 2). The guard has 50% in what guards do best, Close Combat and Perception; 40% in related skills such as Dodge, Resilience and Ranged Combat; 30% or less in the rest. A minor NPC has 10 HP and Combat Order 10 unless the role calls for more.

Level	Typical NPC
30	Frightened villager, untrained thug
40	Bandit, militia
50	Guard, hunter, sellsword
60	Sergeant, assassin, cult leader
70	Champion, master of a craft
CREATURES

Any full-rules creature works as written. Undead and constructs never bleed, breathe, tire or suffer poison; at 0 HP they are destroyed. Threat: roughly as many foes as player characters makes a fair fight. Raise one foe's skill or gear rather than adding more bodies; crowds of weak foes mostly cost time.

COMMON CREATURES

Wolf · HP 12 · MWL 6 · AP 0 · Move 23 m · CO 9 · Dodge 39%, Persistence 33%, Resilience 42%. Bite 50%, 1D8, Medium; Claw 50%, 1D6, Medium.

Bear · HP 19 · MWL 10 · AP 3 (hide) · Move 23 m · CO 8 · Dodge 33%, Persistence 33%, Resilience 39%. Bite 60%, 1D8+2D6, Heavy; Claw 60%, 1D6+2D6, Heavy.

Giant Spider · HP 22 · MWL 11 · AP 4 (chitin) · Move 15 m ground, 23 m on web · CO 12 · Dodge 48%, Persistence 33%, Resilience 51%. Bite 50%, 1D6+1D6, Heavy; Web 50%, special, Heavy, 15 m. Web: Combat Action, Unarmed Combat against Athletics within 15 m; a caught target cannot move and takes -1P. Venom: Potency 51, -6 DEX.

Goblin · HP 9 · MWL 5 · AP 2 (leather) · Move 15 m · CO 11 · Dodge 50%, Persistence 20%, Resilience 35%. Shortspear 40%, 1D6, Medium; Small Shield 40%, 1D4, Medium; Sling 50%, 1D6, 50 m. Blind Sight (heat). Deception 75%.

Orc · HP 13 · MWL 7 · AP 2 (leather) · Move 15 m · CO 8 · Dodge 35%, Persistence 35%, Resilience 35%. Scimitar 40%, 1D8+1D4, Medium; Medium Shield 40%, 1D6+1D4, Heavy; Shortbow 50%, 1D8, 75 m. Adrenaline Surge, as the Orc ancestry.

Skeleton · HP 8 · MWL 4 · AP 2 (leather) · Move 15 m · CO 3 · Dodge 10%, Persistence 100%, Resilience 100%. Arming Sword 35%, 1D8, Medium; Medium Shield 35%, 1D6, Heavy. Mindless undead. Halve piercing damage after armour.

Zombie · HP 7 · MWL 4 · AP 0 · Move 7 m · CO 4 · Dodge 0%, Persistence 100%, Resilience 100%. Fist 50%, 1D3+1D6, Light. Mindless undead.

Ghoul · HP 12 · MWL 6 · AP 0 · Move 15 m · CO 11 · Dodge 40%, Persistence 30%, Resilience 40%. Claw 60%, 1D4+1D4, Medium; Bite 60%, 1D6+1D4, Medium. Howl: listeners within 11 m oppose its Persistence or take -1P to attacks and Reactions. Venom: Potency 22, paralysis.

Ogre · HP 18 · MWL 9 · AP 2 (skin) · Move 15 m · CO 11 · Dodge 35%, Persistence 45%, Resilience 35%. Great Axe 60%, 2D8+2D6, Heavy; Improvised Rock 40%, 1D4+2D6, Light, 23 m; Fist 60%, 1D6+2D6, Light.
